subject: Urgent: Production latency spike — KV cache thrash & HOL blocking
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah@finopsapp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@finopsapp.com
Date: 2026-02-14T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Production: 8x latency increase and 502s — started ~07:50 PST

Marissa —

We started seeing a sudden jump in average token latency and a burst of 502 errors for our user-facing inference path around 07:50 PST. P50 went from ~45ms to ~380ms and error rate spiked to ~3.6% for about 25 minutes. This is affecting billing-recon and the UI is derailing sessions.

We tried re-issuing a few requests and noticed responses hang for a long time (requests appear queued) then fail with 502 from the Redwood endpoint. No config changes on our side. Can you triage? We're on the enterprise Dedicated plan (dedicated pool eu-west-1) but our traffic was routed to us-west for burst.

Example request ids: req_5f7b9a, req_5f7b9b. Logs attached (error snippets).

— Sarah

Thanks Sarah — looping in Dev (serving/runtime) and Evelyn (CS). We're treating this as a priority.

Quick ask: could you confirm the model id and sequence length distribution for the failing requests? If you have a small corpus of request payloads (sanitized) please upload to the Drive link I shared.

Dev/Evelyn — Sarah reports a sharp latency spike and transient 502s coincident with a burst. Initial hypothesis from the logs: HOL (head-of-line) blocking on KV cache misses and cache thrash when traffic moved regions. Can we confirm whether the customer hit a cross-region fallback and whether KV cache warming/consistency could have caused mass misses?

I'll keep the execs updated.

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-14T09:01:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production: 8x latency increase and 502s — started ~07:50 PST

Marissa / Sarah —

I pulled the runtime traces for FinOpsApp's dedicated pool during the incident window. Quick summary:
- Observed a sudden increase in KV cache miss rate (~5% -> ~72%) across the affected nodes at 07:49:33.
- Large coalescing windows and aggressive batching meant a small set of leader requests were holding the event loop and blocking others (classic HOL).
- Because traffic was bursty and spilled to a fallback region, we saw cache shard rehydration requests and lock contention, which caused cache thrash.
- Result: request queuing + timeouts at the serving mesh -> elevated 502s and higher tail latency.

I've attached a short analysis and the error snippets (kv-cache-analysis.pdf and error-rate-log-20260214.txt). Short-term mitigations I recommend immediately:
1) Reduce max_batch_size and lower coalescing_window_ms for this customer's route to avoid large leader batches.
2) Temporarily enable prefix KV caching (keep hot prefixes pinned) and raise the per-shard mem limit to reduce rehydration.
3) Toggle fallback routing to avoid cross-region spill until KV shards have re-synced (force region affinity).

I can push these changes to a canary host in ~15 minutes if Marissa approves. Longer-term: adjust shard placement heuristics and add soft-backpressure to leader batching to avoid HOL.

— Dev Patel
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
attachments: kv-cache-analysis.pdf

From: Sarah Liu <sarah@finopsapp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@finopsapp.com
Date: 2026-02-14T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production: 8x latency increase and 502s — started ~07:50 PST

Thanks Dev — the model was rwd/gpt-medium-16k:v2 and most requests are ~1.2k tokens. We did see the region affinity switch at 07:48:58 in our edge logs — traffic spilled to us-west for ~30 minutes.

Please proceed with the proposed canary changes. We'll hold non-essential traffic on our side and can throttle to test. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Sarah

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-14T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Escalation: Exec brief & mitigation plan

Team —

I spun up a canary with the following changes (applied at 09:33 PST):
- max_batch_size: reduced from 64 -> 18
- coalescing_window_ms: 40ms -> 10ms
- per-shard mem limit: +25% (pin hot prefixes)
- fallback routing: temporarily disabled for the customer's route (region affinity forced)

Immediate result: P50 came down to ~70ms, tails improved, and error rate dropped to ~0.2% within 7 minutes. We still see occasional rehydration logs but no HOL queueing. Attached runbook snippet with rollback steps (runbook-kv-cache.txt).

Executive ask: Sarah is asking for credits and assurance this won't recur. I recommend:
1) Provide a 5% service credit for the incident window.
2) Commit to a follow-up technical remediation: shard placement change + rate-aware batching tweaks in the next sprint.
3) Postmortem (72-hour) with action items and telemetry dashboard for FinOpsApp.

Evelyn — please coordinate the credit/comms. Marissa — can you align with Sarah on the credit and PM next steps? I'll own the tech postmortem.

— Rishi Malhotra
Director, Serving Infrastructure

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah@finopsapp.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>, Troy Carpenter <troy@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-16T17:45:00-08:00
Subject: Post-incident summary & exec next steps — FinOpsApp incident 2026-02-14

Sarah — thanks again for the patience and for coordinating with ops. Summary of outcomes and next steps:

What happened:
- Burst traffic + cross-region fallback caused mass KV cache misses and leader-batch HOL blocking, resulting in increased latency and elevated 502s.

Immediate mitigation applied: (Rishi/Dev) reduced batching and coalescing, increased shard mem for hot prefixes, and forced region affinity. This restored normal latency and error rates within ~10 minutes of the canary roll.

Business actions: (Evelyn) CS will issue a 5% credit covering the incident window (07:48–08:15 PST) and send an official incident notification to your stakeholders.

Technical next steps: (Rishi/Dev) own: shard placement improvements, soft backpressure in leader batching, and a strengthened KV warming strategy. Delivery target: initial fixes in the next 3 sprints; full rollouts and QA over the following quarter.

Postmortem: we'll produce a full 72-hour postmortem with telemetry and runbook updates. I'll follow up with a scheduled readout and a proposed timeline.

If you want an executive-to-executive call, Troy is available to join.

Action items:
- Evelyn: send credit + comms (by 2026-02-17)
- Rishi/Dev: postmortem draft (by 2026-02-18)
- Marissa: schedule E2E readout and confirm credit details with Sarah

— Marissa Cole
